question: Do published taxonomic sources and the MNHN type-series records independently support a fish occurrence in the Simulao River, and what may safely be said about the locality and type specimens?

taxonLead.interpretation: Names are retained as each source displays them. This review is not a fresh taxonomic determination or a complete current-name reconciliation.

2025AnnotatedChecklist.citation: Balisco, R. A. T., & Liao, T.-Y. (2025). An annotated checklist of fish species described from the Philippines. ZooKeys, 1246, 1-287. https://doi.org/10.3897/zookeys.1246.145752.
2025AnnotatedChecklist.reportedTypeLocality: Simulao River, a tributary of Agusan, Mindanao, 1881.
2025AnnotatedChecklist.typeStatusNote: The checklist says the MNHN records indicate holotype and paratypes, and notes that Tan and Husana (2021) referred to the types as syntypes.

2021Redescription.citation: Hui, T. H., & Husana, D. E. M. (2021). Barbodes pyrpholeos, new species, the first cave-dwelling cyprinid fish in the Philippines, with redescription of B. montanoi (Teleostei: Cyprinidae). Raffles Bulletin of Zoology, 69, 309-323. https://doi.org/10.26107/RBZ-2021-0054.
2021Redescription.typeLocalityStatement: The authors state that the type locality is Simulao River in central Mindanao, correcting the spelling Simulac River used by Fricke et al. (2021).
2021Redescription.typeStatusStatement: The authors say the original description was based on 13 individuals and, because Sauvage did not explicitly designate a holotype and no lectotype was designated, they treat the 13 specimens as syntypes under ICZN Article 72.1. They note that MNHN catalogue labels show one holotype and 12 paratypes.
2021Redescription.separateRecentSpecimens: The specimens examined for the redescription were collected from pools at Ugnop and Enchanted Falls; the authors say they likely represent true B. montanoi. They are not the 1881 type series, and this review does not assign those pools to the type locality.
2021Redescription.distributionCaution: The paper says further surveys are needed to clarify the species' true distribution.

mnhnCatalogRecords.accessMethod: Official MNHN record pages were returned with detailed indexed page content by web search. Direct page opens returned a cache-miss error during this review, so page content was not independently re-rendered in the browser tool.

a3398.recordedIdentity: MNHN-IC-A-3398; single specimen; label reads holotype of Puntius montanoi; displayed taxon Barbus montanoi.

a3399.recordedIdentity: MNHN-IC-A-3399; set of 12 specimens; labels read paratypes of Puntius montanoi; displayed taxon Barbus montanoi.

mnhnCatalogRecords.crosswalkLimit: The catalog records do not themselves name Simulao River or provide coordinates. The string 'lag.limao' is preserved verbatim; it is not normalized to a lake, lagoon, river or Simulao site.

reconciliation.locality: The 2021 redescription and 2025 checklist attribute the historical type locality to Simulao River. The MNHN indexed object records expose Mindanao and the waterbody string 'lag.limao', without coordinates or a river name. The site-level crosswalk is therefore unresolved; the sources do not justify turning the catalog strings into a Simulao River geometry or an exact collection point.
reconciliation.typeStatus: The 2021 authors' nomenclatural argument treats all 13 original specimens collectively as syntypes. MNHN catalogue labels and the 2025 checklist describe A-3398 as holotype and A-3399 as 12 paratypes. Both source positions are preserved; this review does not adjudicate the type status.
reconciliation.recentRedescriptionMaterial: The Ugnop and Enchanted Falls pools are later redescription material, not evidence that every named Simulao reach or the entire Agusan basin has current occupancy.

scopeLimits: This is historical taxonomic type-locality evidence from 1881, not a contemporary occurrence or abundance survey.
The type locality does not provide a capture coordinate, station, river reach boundary or usable fishing location.
The record does not establish fish presence throughout Simulao River, the Agusan River, or Region XIII.
The type series and later redescription specimens are distinct evidence and must not be combined as one collection event.
No natural diet, bait, habitat suitability, water quality, safety, catchability, fishing regulation or conservation-status claim is inferred.
The indexed museum records' displayed labels and locality strings are recorded as source metadata; direct-page retrieval was unavailable in the browser tool.
No author, museum, publisher or agency was contacted. No article image, text, table, specimen photograph, bulk dataset or museum media was copied into the repository.

references.supports: 2025 annotated checklist, CC BY 4.0 notice, type-series entries and note contrasting its MNHN labels with the 2021 syntype treatment.
2021 redescription statements on Simulao type locality, original 13-specimen series, syntype argument, separate later specimens and need for further distribution surveys.
Indexed MNHN A-3398 record content, catalogue label and verbatim Mindanao/lag.limao origin fields; direct open was unavailable during this review.
Indexed MNHN A-3399 record content, set of 12 specimens and verbatim Mindanao/lag.limao origin fields; direct open was unavailable during this review.

nextAction: Continue the Caraga inland-water sweep with another independently reviewable primary fish survey or voucher-backed source from a distinct named river, lake or marsh. If pursuing this historical lead, seek an independently cataloged source that explicitly reconciles 'lag.limao' with Simulao and states the basis for the type locality; do not add a site geometry or public occurrence from these records alone.
